The Lovin' Spoonful produced hit after hit, all easily accessible songs that you could sing along with after a few spins. Although you would never use the word "exciting" to describe them, they were very successful, joining Gary Lewis and the Playboys as the only artists in the 1960's to place their first seven singles in the Billboard Top 10.

The band that best exemplifies this latent strain of American Puritanism is The Lovin' Spoonful. Their music is often referred to as "feel-good" music, a fair characterization. Despite folk roots, they never got their feet wet in the sub-genre of protest songs.

Products of the fabled early-'60s Greenwich Village folk scene, The Lovin' Spoonful became the de facto house band of the flower-power era thanks to hippy-dippy hits like "Summer in the City" and "Do You Believe in Magic."
